citations.claim: EW approach E first shows yellow at step 92
EW approach E still yellow at step 93, only 2nd yellow second
EW approach E already red at step 94, so yellow lasted only 2s vs required 4s - first violating step

counterfactual.change: Changed actuated true -> false (fixed-time) keeping all else identical; full yellow timing restored and no violation in 94 steps.

explanation: With actuated=true, EW green held long while NS waited ~70s (recall demand). When EW finally gap-out at step 92 it entered EW yellow, but the actuated recall logic forced the transition to all-red after only 2s (steps 92-93) instead of the required yellow_seconds=4, turning E/W red at step 94. Disabling actuation removes the early truncation, confirming actuated control interrupts/cuts the yellow interval to serve the long-waiting direction.
vision_note: At step 91 two approaches show green, then at steps 92 and 93 those same approaches show yellow. At step 94 all signals are red, so the yellow is cut to only two steps before going red.
